olivia: Quick question — seeing weird behavior when multiple flag scopes match. Example: org: feature_x = true, project: feature_x = false, model: feature_x = true (route not set). In a request that hits project+model, which value should win?

raj: Short answer: most-specific scope wins. We treat route > model > project > org. So in your example model=true should win.

olivia: Ah ok. Is that documented somewhere? I couldn't find the exact ordering in the flag docs.

morgan: Not great if it isn't clear. We historically said "specific overrides default" but didn't list the exact order. I'll open a quick doc PR.

anya: FWIW there are two edge cases to watch: 1) when a route has its own audience canary, and 2) when there are multiple model ids (ensemble). For (1) route-level canary wins because it's the most specific. For (2) we collapse model match rules by precedence among IDs — last-writer for the same scope.

olivia: Good call. Can you paste a tiny pseudocode for how resolution looks? That will help me debug.

raj: Sure — rough:
```
function resolveFlag(flagKey, request) {
  // resolution order: route -> model -> project -> org
  const candidates = [lookup(route, flagKey), lookup(model, flagKey), lookup(project, flagKey), lookup(org, flagKey)];
  for (c of candidates) {
    if (c && c.enabled !== undefined) return c.enabled;
  }
  return defaultValue(flagKey);
}
```

raj: Note: lookup(scope, key) returns the most recent active override in that scope (so if two route-level overrides exist, we pick the one with the higher sequence/created_at).

morgan: One more implementation detail — we treat explicit `null` at a scope as "unset" (fallthrough) to allow removing an override without a delete. That bit confused me earlier when a project-level `null` let org default through.

olivia: That explains what I saw. Thanks.

anya: For rollout guardrails: ensure route-level canaries have percentage checks + a fallback to model/project so if route canary fails we don't flip org defaults. I'd add a lint rule: route canaries must specify a fallback_mode (e.g., `fallback: project` or `fallback: model`).

morgan: I'll add a tiny checklist in the PR: (1) doc the order, (2) unit tests for three-scope combos, (3) example for `null` semantics, (4) note on last-writer at same scope.

olivia: Filing a bug for the specific case I hit: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/issues/1421 — reproducer attached.

raj: Thanks. @morgan please link the PR to that issue.

morgan: On it. PR coming: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/789 — adding tests + docs.

deploy-bot: Scheduled doc deploy to staging docs site tonight at 02:00 UTC.

anya: quick ask — can someone add a tiny debug endpoint that returns the evaluated flag trace for a request (which scope contributed the final value)? Even a read-only trace returned when `?flag_trace=1`. Saves a ton of time.

raj: Good idea. We already have flag-tracing in local fakes; I'll sketch an endpoint in the API that returns something like `{flagKey: [{scope: 'model', value: true, sourceId: 'model-abc'}, ...], final: true}`. Keep it gated behind dev flag.

olivia: Perfect. Thanks all :thumbsup:

morgan: Ack, will follow up in PR comments.

anya: thanks!
